'''Vladimir Alexandrovich Koptsik''' ({{langx|ru| Владимир Александрович Копцик}}; 26{{nbsp}}February 1924 – 2{{nbsp}}April 2005) was a Soviet crystallographer and physicist. In 1966 Koptsik was the first to publish the complete atlas of all 1651 [[Dichromatic symmetry|antisymmetry]] [[Magnetic space group|space groups]].<ref name=atlas>Koptsik, V.A. (1966). ''Shubnikov groups: handbook on the symmetry and physical properties of crystal structures'' (in Russian), Moscow: Moscow University</ref> In 1972 he published ''[[Symmetry in Science and Art]]'' with extensive coverage of [[dichromatic symmetry|dichromatic]] and [[polychromatic symmetry]].<ref name=science_russian >{{cite book | first1=A.V. | last1=Shubnikov | title=Symmetry in science and art | publisher=Nauka | date=1972 | last2=Koptsik | first2=V.A. | location=Moscow | language=Russian}}</ref><ref name=science_and_art>{{cite book | first1=A.V. | last1=Shubnikov | title=Symmetry in science and art | publisher=Plenum Press | date=1974 | last2=Koptsik | first2=V.A. | location=New York | isbn=9780306307591 | language=English}}</ref>

==Life==
===Career===
Koptsik was born on 26 February 1924 in [[Ivanovo]]. In 1941-1944 he worked as a turner in a defence plant in Moscow. Koptsik graduated from [[Moscow State University]] in 1949. He then began post-graduate work under the supervision of [[Alexei Vasilievich Shubnikov|A.V. Shubnikov]] and submitted his candidate's dissertation in 1953.<ref name=obituary>The Editors (2005), ''Vladimir Aleksandrovich Koptsik (February 26, 1924 – April 2, 2005)'', Crystallog. Reports, '''50'''(5), 890-891</ref>

In 1953 Koptsik was hired as an assistant to Shubnikov in the new department of [[Crystallography]] and Crystal Physics at [[Moscow State University|MSU]]. He progressed through various positions, earning his doctorate in 1963, becoming full professor in 1967, and head of department from 1968 to 1974 succeeding Shubnikov.<ref>The Editors (1999), ''Vladimir Aleksandrovich Koptsik (on the occasion of his seventy-fifth birthday)'', Crystallog. Reports, '''44'''(4), 710-712</ref>

Koptsik is known for his contributions to the physics of [[Magnetic space group|electrically and magnetically ordered]] crystals, the [[tensor]] representation of [[Magnetic anisotropy|anisotropic media]], the theory of [[Crystal structure|crystal symmetry]], and the symmetry aspects of structural [[phase transition]]s.<ref>The Editors (1984), ''Vladimir Aleksandrovich Koptsik: sixtieth birthday greeting)'', Crystallog. Reports, '''29'''(3), 371</ref>

From 1966 Koptsik was a member of the Committee on International Crystallographic Tables of the [[International Union of Crystallography]] (IUCr); in 1983 he became a member of the subcommittee on nomenclature of [[Space group#In other dimensions|''n''-dimensional crystallography]].<ref>de Wolff, P. M., Belov, N. V., Bertaut, E. F., Buerger, M. J., Donnay, J. D. H.,  Fischer, W., Hahn, Th., Koptsik, V. A., Mackay, A. L.,  Wondratschek, H., Wilson, A. J. C. and Abrahams, S. C. (1985), ''[https://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/1985/03/00/a24271/a24271.pdf   Nomenclature for Crystal Families, Bravais-Lattice Types and Arithmetic Classes]'', Acta Cryst. A'''41''', 278-280</ref><ref>
Janssen, T., Birman, J.L, Dénoyer, F., Koptsik, V.A., Verger-Gaugry, J.L., Weigel, D., Yamamoto, A., Abrahams, S.C., and Kopsky, V. (2002), ''[https://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/2002/06/00/es0318/es0318.pdf  Report of a subcommittee on the nomenclature of n-dimensional crystallography. II. Symbols for arithmetic crystal classes, Bravais classes and space groups]'', Acta Cryst. A'''58''', 605-621</ref>

===Works===
The majority of Koptsik's works were published in Russian. Books published by Koptsik:

* ''Shubnikov groups: handbook on the symmetry and physical properties of crystal structures'' (1966)<ref name=atlas/>
* ''[[Symmetry in Science and Art]]'' (1972);<ref name=science_russian/> English translation (1974)<ref name=science_and_art/>
* ''Problem exercises for crystal physics'' (1982 and 1988)<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1982 and 1988), ''Problem exercises for crystal physics'', Moscow: Moscow State University</ref>

Koptsik published 300 academic papers.<ref name=obituary/> Selected papers available in English:

* Polymorphic phase transitions and symmetry (1957)<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1957), ''Polymorphic phase transitions and symmetry'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''5'''(6), 889-898</ref>
* A general sketch of the development of the theory of symmetry and its applications in physical crystallography over the last 50 years (1968)<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1968), ''A general sketch of the development of the theory of symmetry and its applications in physical crystallography over the last 50 years'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''12'''(5), 667-683</ref>
* Views of Aleksei Vasil'evich Shubnikov on crystallography and crystal physics (on the ninetieth anniversary of his birth) (1977)<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1977), ''Views of Aleksei Vasil'evich Shubnikov on crystallography and crystal physics (on the ninetieth anniversary of his birth)'', Sov. Phys. Cryst., '''22'''(3), 383-386</ref>
* Symmetry principle in physics (1983)<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1983), ''Symmetry principle in physics'', J. Phys. C:Solid State Phys., '''16''', 23-24</ref>
* Generalized symmetry in crystal physics (1988)<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Koptsik|first1=V.A.|year=1988|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0898-1221%2888%2990231-3|title=Generalized symmetry in crystal physics|format=PDF|journal=Comput. Math. Applic.|volume=16|issue=5–8|pages=407–424|doi=10.1016/0898-1221(88)90231-3 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
* Symmetry bases. The contemporary symmetry theory in solids (1994)<ref>Koptsik, V.A. (1994), ''Symmetry bases. The contemporary symmetry theory in solids'' in ''Advanced mineralogy, vol. 1'', ed. by Marfunin, A.S., 50-55, {{ISBN| 978-3-540-57254-1}}</ref>

===Honours and awards===
* [[E. S. Fedorov]] Prize of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] for his contributions to the theory of [[symmetry]] (1973)
* Honoured Professor of [[Moscow State University]] (1996)
* Honoured Scientist of the [[Russian Federation]] (1999)
